_comment: WI-D15. One fixture per rejection shape the hook-scope split adds, each
PAIRED with a resolving control. A rejection-only suite is passed by a
classifier that resolves nothing -- the `agree=0 disagree=0` shape that has
cost this project two items -- so `verdict: HOOK-PORT-MEDIATED` entries are
load-bearing, not filler.
The pair that carries the READING is control_registration_only /
control_hook_reaches_env: same import, same call, different position. If
they ever agree, the tool has stopped measuring the reading.
ADR-001 Q4 (the default_hooks minor) once had three record-update fixtures
here (control_record_update_*, reject_update_head_not_default_hooks). B8
removed them with the record head: the ABI no longer has `ExtensionHooks` or
`default_hooks`, so the record path, `hook-record-unresolvable` and
`hook-slot-missing` are gone, and every remaining fixture is written in the
6.0 `[Capability]` list shape (eight atoms, in the canonical order, unless
the fixture's purpose is the list itself).
ADR-001 Phase B, B2 (the 6.0 `[Capability]` list head): the four
control_capability_list_* and four reject_capability_list_* fixtures. Every
list control pins its ATOM COUNT -- the fail-closed denominator: a reader
that enumerates fewer atoms than are written cannot report the fixture
green. The named-wide control is the one that carries B1's finding: the
payload row bounds nothing in constructor-argument position, so a wide-rowed
named binding must be SCANNED, and it reaches std/env.
P0.3 (031 ADR-001 D2, the registration-shape gate): every fixture also pins `head`, `shape` and
`shape_reasons` -- RE-PINNED BY HAND. All seventeen are written on the 7.4 bare list, so every
one FAILS the shape by `return-shape-unsupported`, plus whatever its payloads add: the eight-atom
controls bind inline lambdas; `same_kind` let-binds its handle; `binding_unresolvable`'s bare
name resolves nowhere; the four list rejections are `list-not-enumerable`; `computed`'s tail is `caps-computed` too --
neither a record nor a list nor a call, so its head is null. The gate's own fixtures, on the 8.0
head, live in scripts/dst/fixtures/adr001_boundary/gate/ and are run by the same self-test.
P1.7r (031 PLAN-001, ADR-001 D2 on 8.0): FIFTEEN fixtures MIGRATED onto the 8.0 head -- the record
`{ config, caps }` at the registration tail, every payload a NAMED top-level function on its row's
view (`PureCtx`, `AiCtx`, `ProcessCtx`, `ProviderCtx`, `InterceptCtx`), `DescribeTools` on `Json`,
captured registration values disclosed through `config` and decoded from `ext_config` (Amendment 3) --
and re-pinned BY HAND: the walk verdicts and atom counts are unchanged, `head` is `config-caps`,
the shape PASSES wherever the fixture's probe is a walk question (so a passing shape now sits
beside HOOK-AMBIENT and HOOK-UNRESOLVED verdicts: the three layers are distinct), and the four list
rejections plus `binding_unresolvable` fail by their own reason alone, `return-shape-unsupported` gone.
TWO fixtures are KEPT on the 7.4 shape deliberately, because the gate is testing the old form:
`control_capability_list_inline` (the per-atom split over inline lambdas with commas) and
`reject_applied_local` (a capture no named payload can express). Each says so in its header.
Several migrated fixtures do not type-check on 8.0 BY DESIGN (a wide row, `Env`/`Clock` on a rowless
slot, a wrong arity, an unresolvable name); the self-test compiles them only for the std rows and
never asserts the compile -- evidence/P1.7r/CHECKS.log records each one's compiler verdict.

control_registration_only.form: 8.0: registration reads Env and discloses it through `config`; the named hook decodes `ext_config` (the WI-D6 shape under Amendment 3)
control_registration_only.head: config-caps

control_hook_reaches_env.form: 8.0: TWO-SIDED twin of the above -- the same call, in the NAMED hook body
control_hook_reaches_env.head: config-caps

control_named_hook_in_register.head: config-caps

control_ext_ports_call.form: 8.0: property 1's positive half -- AiPorts.ai_step on the Compactor's AiCtx is admitted, not rejected
control_ext_ports_call.head: config-caps

control_interpolated_call.head: config-caps

reject_binding_unresolvable.head: config-caps

reject_unknown_callee.head: config-caps

control_capability_list_empty.head: config-caps

reject_capability_list_element.form: 8.0: one element is a call returning an atom -- a computed element
reject_capability_list_element.head: config-caps

reject_capability_list_arity.head: config-caps

reject_capability_list_unknown_kind.head: config-caps

reject_capability_list_juxtaposed.head: config-caps

_comment: Pinned in BOTH directions over the real seventeen, so a drift in either is a
failure. `closure` is derive.py's shipped answer and must not move: this
item reports a second reading, it does not promote one.
The two sets are NOT nested. Hook scope adds mcp and test_dummy (both the
WI-D6 shape) and DROPS compaction_structural -- not because a hook of it
reaches an effect, but because `show` is a door the shipped tool does not
watch. That drop is the finding, and pinning it here is what keeps it from
being quietly re-admitted.
`capability_list_atoms` (B2) pins, per extension, which registrations
resolve through the 6.0 list head and how many atoms each holds. Empty on
the 5.x tree by construction; B8 re-pinned it BY HAND with seventeen entries
of eight atoms each. Item 4 (6.0 trimming) re-pinned it BY HAND again: each
package now lists only the atoms it binds with a real body (39 over 17).
RE-PINNED BY HAND for EIGHTEEN: `repetition_guard` joined ailang.toml's
[extensions] packages and every pin here was still describing seventeen. It
binds ToolPolicy + SolverJudge with real bodies, so `capability_list_atoms`
gains `repetition_guard: 2` (41 over 18), and it resolves HOOK-PORT-MEDIATED
-- both its hooks reach `ctx` and the world and neither reaches an ambient
source -- so it joins that list rather than `hook_ambient`.
`f` JOINS THE DOOR-3 RESIDUE, and it is a DIFFERENT KIND of gap from the two
already there. `show` and `intToFloat` are language builtins no producer at
HEAD can classify. `f` is not a builtin at all: it is the function-typed
PARAMETER of motoko-ext-herdr's higher-order helpers (`dagr_record`'s
transition callback at herdr.ail:349, `map_task`/`map_last` in dagr.ail), and
an applied parameter has whatever effects its caller passed. The tool is
right that it cannot classify it, and closing it would mean unwinding those
helpers into first-order code -- a worse module for a greener pin. Recorded
as a known gap with its cause rather than assumed away, which is what this
pin is for. It predates the 7.0 work; it is fixed here only because the same
gate was red for the repetition_guard drift.
RE-PINNED BY HAND: `herdr` 4 -> 6. Orchestrator mode
(packages/motoko-ext-herdr/orchestrator.ail) adds PromptShaper + ToolPolicy,
both pure, bound with real bodies, and registered in every configuration (off,
the patch is empty and the policy has no opinion). Measured reason: a session
resumed from a handoff made zero delegations after its predecessor made ten,
because the instruction lived only in a chat turn. The DOOR-3 residue is
unchanged: the one predicate parameter that would have added `p` was written
as direct recursion instead.
P0.3 (031 ADR-001 D2; PLAN-001 P0.3) -- RE-PINNED BY HAND for the 8.0 `{ config, caps }` head.
`capability_list_atoms` now keys on either head and is unchanged: all eighteen still register
through the 7.4 list (45 atoms), which `registration_heads` pins per extension.
`registration_shape_results` pins the gate's own field per extension: all eighteen FAIL on the
unmigrated tree. `shape_binding_rejections` is the MEASURED count the ADR states the tree is red
by -- 35, and it came out 35 (payload-inline-lambda 19, payload-let-bound 16), matching D2's
migration table site for site. P1.2 flips heads and results batch by batch and re-pins by hand.
DOOR-3 RESIDUE LOSES `f`, and this is the signature fix doing what N63 says. `f` was never a
language builtin: it is the function-typed PARAMETER of herdr's higher-order helpers, and it sat
in this residue only because the walk never read a signature. `_params_at` now reads it, so an
applied `f` is `applied-local` (a rejection, as before -- herdr stays HOOK-UNRESOLVED) rather
than `unknown-callee`. The counterfactual list loses herdr for the same reason. `show` and
`intToFloat` remain: those are real producer gaps.
P1.7r (031 PLAN-001) -- RE-PINNED BY HAND after P1.2a-d landed all eighteen packages on 8.0:
`registration_heads` all `config-caps`, `registration_shape_results` all `pass`,
`shape_binding_rejections` 0 (the 35 moved with the batches: A 32, B 18, C 9, D 0 remaining, each
measured at its intake). `capability_list_atoms` is UNCHANGED at 45 over 18 -- the batches replaced
each payload in place and added none -- and was re-counted by hand from each register.ail at HEAD
(evidence/P1.7r/README.md). `hook_port_mediated`, `hook_ambient` and `door_3_residue` did not move.
`closure_port_mediated` IS UNMOVED -- and it was red at HEAD before P1.7r for a reason outside the
extensions: since P0.4 (`f7df893c`) the 8.0 ABI's own view-port projections (`fs_ports`, `ai_ports`,
`intercept_ports`, types.ail:1236-1261) take every ExtPorts field as a VALUE, classifier 2
(tools/ext_call_inventory/derive.py) read that as its form 3, types.ail is in every closure, and the
shipped closure verdict read 0 of 18. P1.7r taught classifier 2 the views (derived by structure),
the same-named projection into a view, and function-scoped binders -- the ambient inventory shares
that scanner -- and the closure came back to exactly these four, measured, so this pin did not move
and was not re-pinned to [] (which would have recorded a classifier that resolves nothing as the
expected state, the `agree=0` shape this file exists to refuse). evidence/P1.7r/BEFORE-AFTER.md.
